findings.title: Current origin/main tip lacks a bound verdict
evidence: No full or abbreviated fbba8af5 commit binding exists in the ledger.
GitHub Actions run 29033274027 warned that fbba8af5ace6 lacked proof and succeeded in report-only mode.
findings.impact: The trunk tip violates the repository's no-verdict-no-done contract while hosted enforcement remains non-blocking.
findings.recommendation: Bind an independently verified verdict and ratchet the backstop to enforcement when operationally ready.

findings.title: Current trunk fails the canonical skill schema gate
evidence: ao gate check --fast --scope head: 68 checks, 66 PASS, 1 FAIL, 1 SKIP; skill.schema failed.
validate-skill-schema.sh rejects intent.mode explicit; 58 of 59 skills pass.
findings.impact: The pinned trunk cannot satisfy its own canonical fast gate and creates pressure to bypass release authority.
findings.recommendation: Correct the goal-design contract and require a green base before further landing.

findings.title: Oversized council verdict line can hide a trailing FAIL
evidence: Three default bufio.Scanner passes neither increase the token limit nor check scanner.Err().
Producer reproduction returned COUNCIL PASS and exit 0 with PASS, a 70000-byte line, and a trailing FAIL.
findings.impact: A verbose or crafted judge artifact can turn a contradictory council into successful verification.
findings.recommendation: Parse once with an explicit maximum and fail on overflow/read error; add the reproduced regression.

findings.title: Tracked executable invokes forbidden claude print mode outside detector coverage
findings.reachability: manual tracked script; no current caller
evidence: bin/ralph directly invokes claude -p with bypassPermissions.
Door 9 scans selected Go paths and passes because tracked shell executables are outside its boundary.
findings.impact: Manual use can violate host LAW 0 and burn the forbidden quota path despite a green dedicated detector.
findings.recommendation: Delete or port the script and cover all tracked production executable surfaces.

findings.title: Legacy Codex dispatcher uses lexical containment across symlink ancestors
evidence: Candidate paths are cleaned and prefix-checked without resolving symlink ancestry.
The implementation and its tests are guarded by //go:build legacy and absent from the default binary.
findings.impact: When the legacy profile is enabled, dispatcher-managed reads/writes can escape declared roots through planted symlink ancestors.
findings.recommendation: Retire the profile or use symlink-aware, directory-relative no-follow path handling with tagged regressions.

findings.title: Legacy Codex required commands bypass sandbox and ignore non-zero exits
evidence: Required commands execute as host sh -c and receipt validation checks presence rather than exit success.
An untagged test command ran zero Codex tests; the behavior is confirmed under go test -tags legacy.
findings.impact: Legacy packets can exceed declared isolation and report successful dispatch after a failed acceptance command.
findings.recommendation: Retire the profile or run commands inside the declared sandbox and fail unexpected non-zero exits.

findings.title: Missing or unreadable changelog clears a blocking fast gate as SKIP
evidence: The native evaluator maps every read error to SKIP, and blocking SKIP does not affect the report exit code.
findings.impact: Deleting a required changelog can pass its dedicated routine gate.
findings.recommendation: Return FAIL for missing/read errors and add deletion/read-error table tests.

findings.title: Supported scripts call removed CLI commands while a baseline keeps the drift gate green
evidence: The current CLI rejects hooks install --force and daemon jobs.
The invocation checker passes because both whole files are grandfathered as current offenders.
findings.impact: Opt-in installation/nightly paths fail after partial work while the targeted drift detector reports PASS.
findings.recommendation: Remove or rewrite dead paths and replace whole-file offender baselines with narrow false-positive exemptions.
findings.prior_status: fresh residue after prior retired-command cleanup

findings.title: Legacy Codex dispatcher lacks bounded output and process-tree termination
evidence: Legacy dispatcher uses unbounded bytes.Buffer outputs and direct-process cancellation; hardened process-group helpers exist elsewhere.
findings.impact: Legacy runs can grow memory without bound or leave descendant processes after timeout.
findings.recommendation: Retire the profile or share a bounded-output, process-group-aware subprocess adapter.

findings.title: Default chaos diagnostic ships stale council fixtures
evidence: Identity validation requires context_id while the built-in pass/fail fixtures omit it, producing a deterministic false council-matrix failure.
findings.impact: A permanently false failure obscures real diagnostic regressions and erodes operator trust.
findings.recommendation: Construct smoke verdicts through a valid shared fixture builder and test the production matrix.

findings.title: Malformed committed verify policy falls back to weaker defaults
evidence: Malformed YAML and typed fields warn and retain defaults; strict defaults false and autobind true.
findings.impact: A repository intending strict verification can silently run a weaker posture after policy corruption or editing error.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed when an existing repository policy cannot be parsed, at least for safety-strengthening keys.

findings.title: Capabilities and REBOUND contracts disagree with executable behavior
evidence: Schema prose says REBOUND does not authorize while the checker authorizes it after lineage proof.
Capabilities omit strict HOLD exit 5, a verify entry, and most environment inputs honored by the CLI.
findings.impact: Agents and generated consumers cannot safely branch from the advertised contract alone.
findings.recommendation: Generate exit/environment declarations from executable sources and reconcile REBOUND semantics.
findings.prior_status: capabilities partially fixed; residual drift persists

findings.title: Canonical architecture docs describe obsolete scale, invariants, and shipped commands
evidence: Fresh measurements are 59 skills, 72 default commands, 112 checks, 363 scripts, and 145 catalog capabilities; several docs advertise archived ao corpus/codex/RPI surfaces.
findings.impact: New operators and agents form an incorrect model before reaching higher-precedence executable surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the first-read pages from current generated inventories and explicitly label tagged archives.

findings.title: MCP surface dispatches an ambient PATH ao binary
evidence: MCP tool execution shells the literal command ao instead of the current executable or an injected trusted path.
findings.impact: A server started from a fresh checkout can execute a stale installed binary with different command or policy behavior.
findings.recommendation: Resolve and pin the trusted running binary, following the ao land freshness pattern.

findings.title: Supported docs-check target invokes a deleted validator
evidence: make docs-check passes CLI reference generation, then exits 127 because scripts/validate-hook-preflight.sh is absent.
The legacy pre-push gate explicitly treats the same validator as intentionally removed in the hookless 3.0 design.
findings.impact: The advertised documentation validation entry point cannot complete and never reaches doc-release validation.
findings.recommendation: Remove the stale Makefile step or replace it with the current hookless safety check, then add a target smoke test.
findings.prior_status: newly promoted; deletion was previously documented but the Make target remained stale
